As usual, you begin by selecting a character, difficulty level, and weapons. Difficulty is straightforward; completing one tier unlocks the next. Characters, however, have unique roles that cater to different playstyles, offering a mix of strengths and weaknesses. The default character is a balanced, all-around option with solid stats and access to any weapon. It’s ideal for new players or those who want a straightforward experience. Additional characters can be unlocked by fulfilling specific, clearly displayed requirements; some through repeated play, others through game progression. Role-specific characters provide more specialized stats. For example, the mage excels with magical abilities but suffers a complete penalty to melee and firearm capabilities. One benefit of choosing a specialized character is the ability to wield two weapons: a role-locked default and one chosen before the run begins. However, weapons are restricted to compatible roles, so you can’t give a boxer a gun, for instance. The gameplay loop is simple and satisfying. Each run takes place in a small arena where you survive waves of enemies until facing a boss. Enemies spawn continuously during each wave until the timer ends. You move around to collect money and experience, while auto-attacks handle the combat. While all money is automatically collected at the end of a wave, picking it up during combat also grants experience, making it worth the effort. Moving around also helps you grab special chests, which provide random item rewards at the end of the wave. Once a wave ends, you're taken to a shop screen. If you found a chest, its contents are revealed first; you can either keep the item or sell it for cash. Most items offer both pros and cons, but it's often wise to keep them. Some, like turrets, are especially valuable. They deploy automatically each wave and help deal with increasingly dense enemy swarms. If you leveled up during the wave, you’ll also get to choose a stat-boosting perk from a random set of four. Then you enter the shop proper, where you can spend money on random weapons or items. You can refresh the selection for a price or lock an item to purchase later. There’s no limit to how many items you can carry, and duplicates stack to enhance their effects. However, you can only equip six weapons at a time. Weapons can be sold or upgraded. If you have two identical weapons of the same rank (out of six possible ranks), you can combine them into a stronger version with better stats. You can't merge weapons of different ranks, even if they’re the same type. The game is enjoyable thanks to its fast pace and rewarding upgrades. You can quickly become powerful and wipe out enemies before they even appear on screen. It’s entirely possible to win your first run on your first try. While there are no permanent upgrades between runs, progress is tracked through in-game achievements. In addition to unlocking new characters, you can also make new items available for future playthroughs.

A high-tempo VS-style shooter featuring an insane number of armed cats running amok. Choose your favorite cat, equip it with synergistic gear, and scatter the approaching hordes of mutants. The visuals are cute and anime-style, but the enemies' attacks are not so cute (they're out to kill you). The game has a random element, so you can enjoy a different experience every time you play. If you like the chaotic mess of games like Vampire Survivors, this is an easy-to-play title for you. とんでもない数の武装猫たちが大暴れする、ハイテンポVS系シューター。お気に入りの猫を選び、シナジーを考慮して強化した装備を整え、迫り来るミュータントの群れを蹴散らしていく。アニメ風のかわいいビジュアル、だが敵の攻撃は割とかわいくない（殺しに来る）。ランダム性があり、毎回異なる展開を楽しめる。『Vampire Survivors』系のごちゃごちゃ系カオスが好きなら、気軽に遊べる作品。 [quote][b]Check out our [url=store.steampowered.com/curator/36364102-Horny-Hentai-Festival/]Steam curator[/url] , [url=www.youtube.com/curatorhhf/]YouTube channel[/url] and [url=x.com/hhfcurator]X(Twitter)[/url]![/b][/quote]

EDIT 2: Changing my review back to RECOMMEND! The devs listened to feedback, and made really nice changes to help with the difficulty curve. EDIT: I have to change my review... at this time, I do not recommend this game. It is simply too hard. Some characters can't even beat the "easiest" difficulty. You constantly get surrounded, while enemies charge attack you, shoot at you, etc. You may make it all the way to the 20th wave (so you've spent at least 30min), only to find that you simply can't beat the final boss, even after 10+ attempts. The final boss is too hard, and very cheap with its attacks (spinning balls of death, and he charges at you). You get hit once and nearly all your life is gone, making any effort to regain health pointless. This game needs major balance work, and hopefully accessibility sliders, where we can adjust the enemy speed and health to our preferred difficulty level. I want to love this game. I want to 100% this game. But at this point that is not possible. There are also major translation issues (some items claim that they *can* do something, where it clearly means to say that they CAN'T do that thing). Original Review: This is literally Brotato with cats and cute 3D graphics, and I’m 100% cool with that. Took me a while to figure out you can pause by pressing B, so I just used Steam’s controller editor to map the B button to the start button. Runs great on the Steam Deck.

It's really as simple as this: Do you like cute cats? Are you looking for a VS-like experience? Are you willing to accept that the arena in this game is really small? Even if you answer yes to only two of these, it's still worthy of a buy and worth the price point. There are a ton of really cute, fun characters that all have their own build gimmick. Items and weapons aplenty. Different game modes and difficulties. Buy it and enjoy these adorable cats.

So, here's the deal. I've been seeing Supercat Survivors pop up on several Youtube gaming creators lists of "Survivors like you must play!" or similarly themed vids, and I dig Survivors games, I dig cats, and Brotato is one of my favorite games - so I of course decided to check this out. First off - If you look at the Steam reviews of Supercat Survivors, you'll see people leaving reviews like, "It's a reskinned Brotato".BUT IT'S MUCH WORSE THAN THAT. They literally use the same stat names, some of the items and weapons are carried over EXACTLY, just given different names. It's not a reskin. It's a cheap knock off. It's not just a reskinned Brotato. It's a buggy, frustrating reskinned Brotato. On the off chance you're reading this not knowing the Brotato formula, it's an arena shooter/survivor game, where you have a class that has different abilities, and you choose from a variety of weapons to survive an Arena for X amount of rounds. You have a shop and drops in the levels to give you random items to power yourself up, and you eventually get a boss, and win the game. There are multiple difficulty levels, a lot of classes and build options, and other game modes to keep you coming in. Honestly, it's basically a puzzle game - as the challenge comes from finding the items and builds that work with the class you chose, and then making it happen. This comes to my first major gripe, that's not SPECIFICALLY about Supercat, but the genre as a whole. In order to unlock ALL the items possible, for many of these games (Brotato and Supercat included) - You have to beat the game with EVERY Class. Which takes roughly 30 minutes per char if you know what you are doing, and with 40ish chars in each game, well you do the math. That's what you have to do just to unlock all the items in the game so that you can start PLAYING THE GAME. This is too much time to commit to a title that's supposed to be an arcade game and casual friendly. Now, if the game is GOOD, and you enjoy playing it, and plan to play it and challenge yourself after the fact, one could argue it's worth going through this rigamarole (IE - BROTATO) - But if the game is mediocre, or SLIGHTLY worse than the best game in the genre, you are wasting way too much time to actually be able to play the game in full, which I FREAKING DID. Now - Here's my quick list of why this is worse than Brotato gameplay wise: The controls aren't as smooth. You can't manually aim. The arena is too small and repetitive. The enemies aren't visually interesting. The bosses lack variety. The hit boxes are awful, making Melee weapons particularly unfun to use. The weapons don't do enough to differentiate themselves when you're using then. The action is a little too fast, the arena is crowded, making it very difficult to know what's actually happening. Oh yea, you HAVE to use a mouse to be able to see everything and get tooltips. The weapons and effects just don't feel satisfying. And THIS IS MORE EXPENSIVE THAN BROTATO!!!! Oh, and BUGS. Bosses get stuck and stop moving. The game crashes. Just scrolling through menus, there are items you literally can't move side to side to, you have to go around and up to select them. Some of the gametextisactuallywithoutspaceslikethismakingithardtoread. Some items don't work correctly and don't calculate stats and bonuses well. So basically, the coder said, "Brotato is popular, how do I do that and make money?" and defaulted to cats, because, internet. IT'S NOT ALL BAD KIDS - There ARE actually a couple things I like, and :gasp: a couple improvements over the Brotato forumla. The main one is that there are different game modes, and seasonal content. There are high scores for a couple different modes though even then, a high score in a game like this basically means watching someone else figure out the best class/combo and then praying to RNJesus that you get the items needed to make it work. HOWEVER, there is a new mode called Fusion which allows you to play two classes together, which is fun and cool. The monsters that carry items are visually easy to see in this game as opposed to Brotato. Some of the items and systems are simplified, and some items that are useless in Brotato are NOT in Supercat. These are good things. So, if you are drawn to this game, and have not played Brotato, PLAY BROTATO. If you are sick of Brotato, at least play a knock off that is trying to be different (Gunbot Diplomacy, for example). DO NOT REWARD THIS KNOCK OFF. I am literally not even sure how they haven't been sued. And content creators, STOP PROMOTING THIS GARBAGE. Just like the game itself, I have spent way more time on this review than I planned. Is it ALL bad? No. Is it good? No. Is it a blatant ripoff and should not be rewarded with your time and money? Yes.

SuperBro Cat-ato is a dumbed down kid friendly version of Brotato with a cute skin. It's not challenging in the slightest, and I expected the items to be cat themed as well as the weapons, but they weren't. There is an accessibility setting to make it easier/harder if you so desire. If you really really really enjoyed Brotato and want another game thats literally the same thing then go for it. Otherwise, play Brotato.
